claims.text: The general aggression model serves as a useful theoretical framework for understanding cyberbullying.
Normative beliefs about aggression are among the strongest associations with cyberbullying perpetration.
Moral disengagement is among the strongest associations with cyberbullying perpetration.
Stress is among the strongest associations with cyberbullying victimization.
Suicidal ideation is among the strongest associations with cyberbullying victimization.
Methodological and sample characteristics serve as moderators of relationships between cyberbullying and behavioral/psychological variables.

evidence.description: The general aggression model is proposed as a useful theoretical framework from which to understand this phenomenon.
Mixed effects meta-analysis results indicate that among the strongest associations with cyberbullying perpetration were normative beliefs about aggression
Mixed effects meta-analysis results indicate that among the strongest associations with cyberbullying perpetration were... moral disengagement
the strongest associations with cyberbullying victimization were stress
the strongest associations with cyberbullying victimization were... suicidal ideation.
Several methodological and sample characteristics served as moderators of these relationships.

methodologies.name: Mixed-effects meta-analysis
methodologies.description: A meta-analytic review examining cyberbullying research among youth to synthesize relationships with behavioral and psychological variables.

limitations.text: Existing cyberbullying literature is highly fragmented and lacks theoretical focus.
Meta-analytic associations face issues dealing with causality or directionality.
Generalizability is limited for meta-analytic estimates based on smaller sets of studies (k < 5).

future_work.text: Understand the incremental impact of cyberbullying over and above traditional bullying on key behavioral and psychological outcomes.
